EmptyParams.description: Parameters of a method that takes none: `{}`.

abi.description: Always `ABI`; a host refuses an engine whose ABI differs.

features.description:
Opt-in behaviours this engine supports, e.g. `action-report`. Absent
from older engines: read as `[]`.

showCursor.description: Display-only virtual cursor; never changes input admission.

allowHostRelayOnlyStop.description: Accept a heartbeating host relay as the only stop path.

auditPath.description: Audit JSONL file; `None` turns auditing off.

reportMode.description:
`object` makes every mutating request return an `ActionReport` and its
errors carry `disposition`; send it only to an engine whose
`engine.hello` lists `action-report`.

intervention.description: What a background action does when the user is using the target app.

macosKeyPriming.description: macOS background key priming; accepted and stored, not acted on yet.

trace.description:
Per-stage `timings` in action reports, and with `auditPath` a
redacted JSONL trace in its `trace/` directory.

MacosCanaryMode.description: Whether macOS verifies background delivery before the session's first input.

coordinateSafe.description: Clamp to the coordinate-safe size for models that click in image pixels.

maxBytes.description: Inline byte budget; above it the capture degrades to JPEG, then artifact-only.

ReportMode.description:
What a mutating request returns: `null` (protocol 1 default) or an
`ActionReport`.

InterventionPolicy.description: What a background action does when the user is using the target app.

KeyPriming.description: Whether macOS background keys first make the target window key.

SessionOpenResult.description:
`session.open` reply. `resume_token` is the only way to lift a stop latch
(`stopPath.resume`) and is never forwarded past the host process.

cursorOverlay.description: Whether the display-only virtual cursor is live now.

focusGuard.description: Whether foreground delivery restores the previous front window and cursor.

stopReason.description: Why the stop path is not `global`, when it is not.

integrityLevel.description: Windows mandatory integrity level of the engine process.

displayAsleep.description:
Every display the session can capture is asleep (macOS; read live on
each `capabilities` call). Other backends always report `false`.

legacyCapture.description:
Captures run through the legacy `screencapture` path, not the
ScreenCaptureKit worker (B9: macOS < 14, helper missing, or the
helper failed to start).

interventionWatch.description:
The watch of the user's own key presses and clicks in the apps the
session works in; absent on backends without one.

windowInput.description: Whether window-addressed input works here, and why not (object mode).

DesktopCapabilities.description:
Runtime truth about what this host's backend can do right now.

Schema-backed field set; additions update Rust, generated schema and TS together.

oneOf.description: Watching: every key press and click the user makes is recorded.

The system refused the watch: nothing is watched, and background
input is not held back for it.
No request has read or acted on an app yet.

InterventionWatch.description:
The state of the backend's watch of the user's own input (macOS: a
listen-only event tap). It starts with the session's first request that
reads or acts on an app.

WindowInput.description:
Window-addressed input availability; `reason` is an open token set
(`no_eis`, `portal_missing`, `kwin_dbus_missing`,
`gnome_extension_missing`).

ControlGrantParams.description:
`control.grant`: `confirmationId` is the host's receipt of the human
confirmation it showed; the engine never sees the confirm itself.

grantedAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, matching the audit timestamps.

ControlStateResult.description:
`control.grant` and `control.state` reply: this session's live foreground
control grant. `reason` and `granted_at` are present exactly when
`active` is true.

DesktopDisplay.description:
Monitor geometry in both global logical desktop coordinates and composite
screenshot pixels.

id.description:
Backend-defined opaque window id, valid as a capture target while the
window lives. Numeric on X11/Win32/macOS; a composite AT-SPI string on
Wayland (e.g. `atspi::1.31:/org/a11y/atspi/accessible/1`). Never parse
it.

title.description: Window title; may be empty for untitled windows.

pid.description: Owning process id when the platform exposes it.

focused.description: Whether the window currently holds input focus.

isOnScreen.description:
Whether the window is on the active Space. `None` on backends that
cannot tell (X11/Win32/Wayland report every listed window on screen).

elevated.description:
Whether the owning process runs above the engine's integrity level
(Windows); `None` where the platform has no such notion.

identity.description:
Who owns the window, so a reused window number is told apart (object
mode).

DesktopWindow.description:
One capturable top-level window in global logical desktop coordinates.
`is_on_screen` distinguishes an on-Space window from a same-app window on
another Space: both resolve as capture targets, but only an on-screen one
is user-visible right now.

WindowIdentity.description:
A window's identity: its number plus the owning process and that
process's start time (`null` where the OS has none).

excludeWindowTitles.description: Titles of windows to exclude from a display capture.

CaptureParams.description:
`capture`: one target (`desktop` or a window id) under optional caps.
`excludeWindowTitles` applies to display captures only: every window with
a matching title is left out of the screenshot (B9, macOS ScreenCaptureKit;
empty elsewhere and ignored by older engines).

data.description: Base64 image bytes when `mode` is inline.

isOnScreen.description:
The captured window's on-Screen state (macOS B9; absent for desktop
captures and backends that cannot tell).

legacyCapture.description:
`true` when this capture ran through the legacy `screencapture`
fallback instead of the ScreenCaptureKit worker (B9).

identity.description: The captured window's identity at capture time (object mode).

CaptureMode.description: How a capture was delivered under the byte budget.

CaptureRegion.description: Rectangle in the pixels of the last full screenshot, not the zoom image.

CaptureRegionParams.description: `captureRegion`: native-detail zoom preserving the last full input frame.

ObserveParams.description: `observe`: an atomic window screenshot and accessibility snapshot.

since.description: Only nodes changed since this generation.

skeleton.description: Roles and refs only, no values.

data.description: Base64 image bytes when `mode` is inline.

isOnScreen.description:
The captured window's on-Screen state (macOS B9; absent for desktop
captures and backends that cannot tell).

legacyCapture.description:
`true` when this capture ran through the legacy `screencapture`
fallback instead of the ScreenCaptureKit worker (B9).

identity.description: The captured window's identity at capture time (object mode).

ObserveResult.description: One delivered window observation; capture pixels remain the input frame.

frameId.description:
When present it must name the target's latest capture frame, otherwise
the call fails `InvalidCoordinateFrame`.

PointParams.description: `click` / `moveMouse`: a point in the pixels of the target's latest frame.

consume.description: After this action the frame may not be used for input again.

route.description: Absent when the engine does not name the channel.

timings.description: Per-stage durations; only in a session opened with `trace: true`.

auditIds.description: Ids of the `audit` notifications this request emitted.

ActionReport.description:
Result of a mutating request in a session opened with
`reportMode: "object"`.

Disposition.description: Whether input reached the target, and whether sending the same request again could duplicate it. Five delivery classes, seven (delivery, retry) pairs.

oneOf.description: Nothing reached the target. `safe`: sending again cannot duplicate input; `after_user`: only after the human acts (resume, permission, unlock, a control grant, a pause in their own typing).
Input may have reached the target. `unsafe`: sending again may duplicate it; `unknown`: the engine cannot tell. Read the target first.
Input was delivered, in full or up to `delivered.count`, and its effect was not read back.
Input was delivered in full and its effect was read back.
The engine cannot say what happened: an internal error, an epoch change during input, a reply quarantined after a stop, or an engine restart.

count.description: Units delivered: Unicode scalars for typed text.

oneOf.description: Only in SDK batch reports, never in an engine reply.

ActionEffect.description: What a read-back of the target showed.

label.description: `null` for a secure field or an element without a label.

ActionHit.description: The element under the point before input was sent.

FocusRestoration.description: The front window and key window after the action.

NextCall.description: The suggested next request; never followed automatically.

Method.description: Every engine method, by wire name.

axResolve.description: Resolving an accessibility ref to its element.

capture.description: Capturing the focus and cursor state the request restores.

prime.description: Making the target window key before background keys.

verify.description: The checks after the input was sent.

StageTimings.description:
How long each stage of one mutating request took, in microseconds. A
stage the request did not run is absent.

DragParams.description: `drag`: a pointer path in the pixels of the target's latest frame.

ScrollParams.description: `scroll`: wheel deltas at a point in the target's latest frame.

force.description: Sends a chord the engine treats as dangerous (`cmd+q`, `alt+f4`).

HoldKeysParams.description: `holdKeys`: keys are always released before the request settles.

HoldMouseParams.description: `holdMouse`: coordinates address the latest full capture, never a zoom.

MenuPathParams.description:
`menus.items`: the window whose menu is addressed and the path inside it
(empty lists the menu bar). `menus.select` takes [`MenuSelectParams`].

MenuItem.description:
One immediate child of a native application menu. `path` holds the native
labels, ellipses included; selection accepts normalized labels.

MenuSelectParams.description:
`menus.select`: the window, the 1..=32-label path to a command, and the
delivery. An omitted delivery is background; `foreground` raises and keys
the target window and needs this session's live control grant (#9888).

generation.description: The ref generation this snapshot registered (object mode).

parent.description: The generation this drill-down snapshot hangs under (object mode).

complete.description: Whether every node under the root was read (object mode).

nodesObserved.description: Nodes read, including those left out of `text` (object mode).

cuts.description: The nodes whose children were cut (object mode).

AxCut.description:
A node whose children the snapshot left out; its text line renders as
`[... <childCount> more]`.

evidence.description: How each field was obtained (object mode).

subtreeTruncated.description: The walk stopped above this node's children (object mode).

secure.description: A secure text field: its value is never read (object mode).

EvidenceState.description:
`known`: read and present; `absent`: read and not there; `unknown`: not
read (timeout, error, or withheld for a secure field).

AxElementAtParams.description: `ax.elementAt`: hit-test at global logical desktop coordinates.

AxTypeTextParams.description:
`ax.typeText`: types `text` into the element `ref` names. Only
`opts.deliveryMode` is read: an omitted delivery is background (no focus
change for the user); `foreground` raises the element's window under the
control grant, like `ax.click`.

report.description: The action report, in a session opened with `reportMode: "object"`.

oneOf.description:
Written through the element's own selection (`AXSelectedText` on
macOS) and read back exactly; no key was sent and no focus moved.

Sent as keystrokes once the element held its application's keyboard
focus.

StopPathStartParams.description:
`stopPath.start`: the stop chord the Global listener arms, e.g.
`ctrl+alt+shift+escape`.

reason.description:
Why input is not allowed, when it is not (e.g. `no-global-listener`,
`heartbeat-stale`).

StopPathKind.description: Which stop path currently guards input.

StopPathResumeParams.description:
`stopPath.resume`: the per-process token only the `session.open` reply
carries.

RequestId.description: A JSON-RPC request id: a number or a string, echoed verbatim.

AdvanceClockParams.description: `$/test.advanceClock`: moves the injected fake clock forward.

textDelivered.description:
Fully delivered Unicode scalars; may be shorter than `text_length`
when a stop or cancellation interrupts typing.

textSha256.description:
First 16 hex digits of the typed text's SHA-256; the text itself is
never audited.

id.description: Names this event in an `ActionReport.auditIds` (object mode only).

AuditEvent.description: The `audit` notification: one per mutating request, success or failure.

oneOf.description: A request aborted by `$/cancel` or a host abort.

Another session holds the foreground control grant. The slot is never
stolen; the caller can retry after it releases.
Foreground delivery without this session's live control grant.

The capture target exists but cannot be captured right now; `data`
says why (e.g. `{ "reason": "minimized" }`).

The user was using the target app, or brought another window to the
front, before or during the action, so the action stopped; the message
says whether any input was sent. Read the window again once the user
pauses; never repeat the action blindly.

An accessibility request was made, but the app did not confirm its
outcome (it did not reply in time or messaging failed, e.g. while the
action opened a modal dialog). It may already have taken effect: read
the element back before any retry.

Moving a window between Spaces is not available on this backend or OS
version.

The window server refused the Space move, or the move could not be
verified.

A target description matched more than one window or element; the
caller must name one of the candidates.
Capturing this target needs the user's consent first.
The target process is protected: the engine never sends it input.

ErrorCode.description:
Desktop error vocabulary shared by the engine, the wire, and the host.

FROZEN: oh-my-pi's codes plus the stop-path, suspension, lock-screen,
cancellation, and restore-transaction codes. Adding a code needs a plan
amendment because the TS protocol and numeric JSON-RPC codes derive from it.
The enum is append-only: a new code takes the next ordinal, so no existing
numeric code moves. Amendment 1 (macOS shared-screen parity, #11459 /
#11461) appended `UserIntervened`, `AxUnconfirmed`, `SpaceUnsupported` and
`SpaceMoveDenied` (-32024..-32027) without a protocol version change.
Amendment 2 (computer-use v2 P1a) appended `AmbiguousTarget`,
`CaptureConsentRequired` and `ProtectedProcess` (-32028..-32030), also
without a protocol version change.

EpochReason.description: Why earlier frames, refs and beliefs about the desktop no longer hold.

RpcRequest.description:
A client request, or a client notification when `id` is absent
(`$/cancel`). `method` stays a string so unknown names parse and get
rejected with `-32601`.

RpcFailure.description: `id` is `null` only when the request id could not be read (parse error).

hint.description: Recovery hint for the model, e.g. `capture it again`.

reason.description:
Machine-readable cause, an open token set per code (object mode),
e.g. `InvalidCoordinateFrame`: `resized`, `consumed`, `zoom`,
`wrong_target`, `out_of_bounds`; `WindowNotFound`: `identity_changed`;
`InvalidTarget`: `ambiguous`; `BackgroundUnavailable`:
`key_route_unproven`, `user_active_in_target`,
`pointer_reading_toolkit`, `electron_select`,
`wayland_window_targeting`; `InvalidKey`: `dangerous_chord`;
`ControlRequired`: `headless_host`, `spawn_inside_session`,
`lease_missing`; `Suspended`: `stop_marker`; `Internal`:
`request_too_large`, `other`.

disposition.description: Whether input reached the target (object mode).

CaptureUnavailableData.description:
Why a `CaptureUnavailable` capture was refused. `reason` is an open token
set: B9 introduces `"minimized"`; P8 adds `"off-space"` and `"off-screen"`; later waves add more.

oneOf.description: Not in the method table.
A bridge (`--oneshot`) refused a host-only method.
A test-only method without `SENPI_DESKTOP_FAKE_CLOCK=1`.

Notification.description: Every server-to-client notification, by wire name.
